images.title: Kanti's lines and John's lines for 26 × 13
images.purpose: Show that Kanti's four lines and John's two lines hold the same four small products for 26 × 13, so that only the layout is different.
images.composition: Two panels side by side with the same top lines 26 (20 + 6) and × 13 (10 + 3): Kanti's four lines on the left, John's two lines on the right, each small product in the same colour in both panels, and the total 338 at the bottom of each.
images.exact_structure: Plain white frame, 1456 by 816. Two panels side by side, each a rounded rectangle (corner radius 20 px) with a grey #6B7280 outline (3 px) and white fill: the left panel spans x 60 to 700 and y 90 to 700, the right panel spans x 756 to 1396 and y 90 to 700. Inside each panel, centred at the panel's middle (x 380 on the left, x 1076 on the right) and y 140, a title in dark #1F2937 bold sans-serif (38 px): Kanti's four lines on the left and John's two lines on the right. Under each title, centred at the panel's middle in dark bold sans-serif (40 px): at y 215 the text 26 (20 + 6) and at y 270 the text × 13 (10 + 3), then a dark #2B2B2B rule (3 px) at y 292 from 140 px inside the left edge to 140 px inside the right edge of the panel. FOUR SMALL PRODUCTS, each with its own colour in both panels: 18 is teal #0072B2, the first 60 (from 3 × 20) is amber #E69F00, the second 60 (from 10 × 6) is green #009E73, and 200 is reddish purple #CC79A7. LEFT PANEL: four rounded chips, each 380 px wide and 56 px tall, centred at x 380, one under the other at y 350, 420, 490 and 560 (centres); chip 1 is teal with white text 18 (3 × 6); chip 2 is amber with dark text 60 (3 × 20); chip 3 is green with white text 60 (10 × 6); chip 4 is purple with dark text 200 (10 × 20). A dark rule (3 px) at y 610 and, centred at x 380 and y 660, the text 338 in bold (44 px). RIGHT PANEL: two lines. Line 1 (centre y 380): a teal chip (90 by 56 px) with white text 18, the sign +, an amber chip (90 by 56 px) with dark text 60, then the plain text = 78 (3 × 26). Line 2 (centre y 480): a green chip (90 by 56 px) with white text 60, the sign +, a purple chip (110 by 56 px) with dark text 200, then the plain text = 260 (10 × 26). A dark rule (3 px) at y 610 and, centred at x 1076 and y 660, the text 338 in bold (44 px). Centred at x 728 and y 760 the caption The same four small products in dark #1F2937 bold sans-serif (38 px). In all there are 4 chips in the left panel and 4 chips in the right panel, the same four colours. No other text. Nothing else in the frame.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
a left panel with a number of lines other than 4 or a right panel with a number of lines other than 2
a small product that has a different colour in the two panels, or a total other than 338
images.takeaway: The same four small products, 18, 60, 60 and 200, sit in four lines for Kanti and in two lines for John, and both add to 338.
images.description: Two panels for 26 × 13: four coloured lines 18, 60, 60 and 200 on the left, and two lines 18 + 60 = 78 and 60 + 200 = 260 on the right, both ending in 338.
images.context: Concept image for Write the Parts in Lines. It follows the idea of Kanti's and John's solutions in your maths book (the same product written in four lines and in two lines) and uses the numbers of this concept's own example: 26 and 13.
images.teaching_notes: Let the student match each colour in John's lines to a line of Kanti's. The slip to watch: writing the small products without their zeros, for example 6 instead of 60.

image_decisions.why: The two layouts side by side, with the same colours for the same products, show what is the same and what is different, which words alone do not.
